missing_requirements.title: Dates of Service Generalization / Shifting Invariant
missing_requirements.description: The pipeline must shift or truncate all ages over 89 and dates related to individuals (except year) to comply with HIPAA Safe Harbor date aggregation rules, preventing indirect re-identification through temporal precision.
missing_requirements.justification: Step 1: HIPAA Safe Harbor requires removing or generalizing explicit dates and ages over 89. Step 2: The Pass 1 requirements only cover the 18 direct identifiers but omit temporal attributes like exact timestamps and ages which act as quasi-identifiers. Step 3: Therefore, a specific transformation guard for dates and ages must be enforced to prevent structural non-compliance.

missing_requirements.title: Pipeline Failure Recovery and Partial Ingestion Poison Pill Protection
missing_requirements.description: The pipeline must implement atomic transaction boundaries and dead-letter queue (DLQ) routing for records failing de-identification parsing, ensuring malformed or non-compliant records never leak into the analytics store.
missing_requirements.provenance: Data Engineering and HIPAA Minimum Necessary Standard
missing_requirements.justification: Step 1: Export pipelines processing sensitive health data encounter malformed records or parsing exceptions. Step 2: Unhandled exceptions during stripping can lead to partial flushes or unredacted payloads bypassing the audit step. Step 3: Hence, a robust failure isolation mechanism (DLQ/atomic rollback) is mandatory to guarantee zero unredacted leaks upon pipeline crashes.

missing_requirements.title: Downstream Re-identification Risk & Quasi-Identifier Constraint Check
missing_requirements.description: The pipeline must evaluate residual re-identification risk (e.g., k-anonymity checks) for rare demographic combinations even after the 18 direct identifiers are stripped.
missing_requirements.justification: Step 1: Safe Harbor mandates stripping 18 identifiers, but sparse combinations of remaining attributes can still uniquely identify individuals. Step 2: Relying solely on strict Safe Harbor stripping without verifying composite uniqueness leaves residual exposure to linkage attacks. Step 3: Therefore, a secondary safeguard validating quasi-identifier distribution is necessary for rigorous data protection.
